Below is a taxonomy built only from the rules you provided. I group the puzzles by the main thing the solver is asked to construct or assign on the grid, and then note important secondary rule features where useful.

# Taxonomy of the listed grid-based logic games

## I. Cell-state puzzles
Puzzles where the main action is to decide the state of cells: black/white, shaded/unshaded, bulb/no bulb, symbol choice, etc.

### I.A. Binary shading / coloring of cells
Cells are typically black vs white, shaded vs unshaded.

#### I.A.1. Shading with connectivity constraints on one color
- **Heyawake**  
  Paint cells; black cells cannot touch orthogonally; white cells must stay connected; room counts and “no more than two rooms in a straight line” rule.
- **Hitori**  
  Color cells black so duplicates disappear in rows/columns; black cells cannot touch orthogonally; white cells must be connected.
- **Kurodoko**  
  Color cells black; numbered cells stay white; black cells cannot touch orthogonally; white cells must be connected.
- **Usowan**  
  Color cells; numbered cells stay white; black cells cannot touch orthogonally; white cells must stay connected; one wrong clue per room.

#### I.A.2. Shading with connectivity constraints on black cells / wall formation
- **Nurikabe**  
  Fill cells black/white; numbered white islands of given size; black cells form one continuous wall; no 2×2 black.
- **Nuritwin**  
  Shade cells; shaded cells must be connected across regions; each region contains exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; no 2×2 shaded.
- **LITS**  
  Shade tetrominoes, one per region; shaded cells must be connected; no 2×2 shaded; same tetromino shape may not touch edge-to-edge across regions.
- **Sto-stone**  
  Fill colored cells black; black cells cannot connect across room borders before “dropping”; after dropping, stones fill bottom half without gaps.

#### I.A.3. Shading with local clue counts
- **Akari**  
  Place bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells count adjacent bulbs; illumination constraints.
- **Kurotto**  
  Color cells black; circles stay white; circle number gives sum of continuous black cells extending orthogonally.
- **Yajilin**  
  Shade black cells and draw a loop; arrow-number clues count black cells in a direction; black cells cannot touch orthogonally.
- **Tilepaint**  
  Color whole tiles black or white; diagonal-number clues count black cells to the right/down until boundary or another clue cell.

#### I.A.4. Shading with shape restrictions on black and/or white regions
- **Choco Banana**  
  Black connected cells must always form a rectangle/square; white connected cells must not form a rectangle/square; numbers give area size.
- **Shakashaka**  
  Place triangular black halves in cells; remaining white parts must form rectangles/squares.
- **Nurimisaki**  
  Fill cells black/white; circled cells are white “promontories” with degree 1 in white network; white connected; neither color may form 2×2.
- **Nurimeizu**  
  Paint whole rooms black or leave white; white cells form a maze from S to G; white cannot be cut off or form a loop; no 2×2 monochromatic blocks.

### I.B. Non-binary symbol placement in cells
Cells receive symbols or marks rather than just black/white.

- **Juosan**  
  Fill every cell with either — or |, with territory balance clues and run-length restrictions by orientation.
- **Evolomino**  
  Draw squares in some white cells; connected square groups form blocks tied to arrows and growth-by-one evolution rule.
- **Hebi**  
  Place numbers 1–5 in white cells as snakes; snakes cannot touch; directional visibility constraints from snake heads and arrow clues in black cells.

### I.C. Number placement in cells
The main task is assigning numbers to cells.

#### I.C.1. Latin / room-based number placement
- **Sudoku**  
  Fill 1–9 so each row, column, and 3×3 box contains all digits 1–9.
- **Makaro**  
  Fill rooms with 1 up to room size; arrow clues indicate largest adjacent number in arrow direction; equal numbers cannot touch across rooms.
- **Ripple Effect**  
  Fill rooms with consecutive numbers from 1; equal numbers in a row/column must be spaced at least their value apart.

#### I.C.2. Region-size number placement
- **Fillomino**  
  Partition into same-number regions; region size equals the number; equal-sized regions cannot touch orthogonally.

#### I.C.3. Sequence / list fitting
- **Nansuke**  
  Fill blank cells with numbers from a given list; entries run horizontally or vertically.

---

## II. Region-partition puzzles
Puzzles where the main task is to divide the grid into regions/blocks by drawing borders or inferring partitions.

### II.A. Partition into arbitrary regions with size/shape rules
- **Five Cells**  
  Divide grid into blocks of exactly five cells; clues count bordering lines around a cell.
- **Shikaku**  
  Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains one number equal to its area.
- **Sashigane**  
  Divide grid into one-cell-wide L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends and may give size; arrows mark ends pointing toward bend.
- **Double Choco**  
  Divide grid into blocks; each block contains matching white and gray areas of same shape/size, possibly rotated/reflected; number gives half-block count of that color.

### II.B. Partition implicit through shaded blocks
These are partly shading puzzles, but the core structure is region/block formation.
- **Chained Block**  
  Fill cells black/white; consecutive black cells form blocks; each block has one clue or ?; corner-touching blocks form chains; no chain may contain duplicate size-and-shape blocks.
- **Norinori**  
  Place black cells in dominoes; each outlined area contains exactly two black cells.
- **Nuritwin**  
  Each region contains exactly two shaded blocks of equal size.
- **LITS**  
  Each outlined area contains one tetromino.

---

## III. Loop-drawing puzzles
Puzzles where the main object is a single loop drawn through cells or along grid edges.

### III.A. Loop through cell centers
The loop runs through cells, horizontally/vertically, sometimes turning.

#### III.A.1. Pure loop with local clue behavior
- **Masyu**  
  Single loop through all circles; white circles force straight passage with adjacent turn; black circles force turn with straight continuation.
- **Mid-loop**  
  Single loop through all black circles; each black circle is midpoint of a straight segment.
- **Dotchi-Loop**  
  Single loop through cells; must include white circles, exclude black circles; within each bold area, all white circles are all-straight or all-turning.
- **Moon-or-Sun**  
  Single loop; each room entered only once; in each room loop uses all moons or all suns, alternating type between consecutive rooms.
- **Nagareru**  
  Single directed loop; must pass arrow cells; wind from black-arrow cells constrains movement direction and bending.
- **Suraromu**  
  Single loop through cells; must pass all gates exactly once each; open circle gives number of gates traversed; numbered gate ends specify traversal order.
- **Yajilin**  
  Single loop through non-black, non-number cells; combined with black-cell placement.

### III.B. Loop on grid edges
- **Slitherlink**  
  Draw a single loop along edges between dots; numbers count incident edges around cells.

---

## IV. Path / connection puzzles without a single loop
Puzzles where the main task is connecting endpoints or routing paths, but not necessarily one loop.

### IV.A. Pair-connection paths
- **Numberlink**  
  Connect matching numbers with non-crossing, non-branching paths through cells.

### IV.B. Directed or endpoint-emitting paths
- **Pencils**  
  Mark pencils and draw a line from each tip; pencil length is given by numbers in pencil cells; line length matches pencil length; lines do not branch/cross themselves.
- **Yosenabe**  
  Move circles by straight arrows into gray areas; arrows do not bend or cross; gray-area sums match incoming circle numbers.
- **Satogaeri**  
  Move circles orthogonally so each country ends with one circle; numbered circles move exactly that many cells; paths cannot cross or pass over circles.

### IV.C. Maze / route existence under shading
- **Nurimeizu**  
  Create a white maze from S to G while deciding room shading; shortest-path conditions for circles and triangles.

---

## V. Object-placement / geometric construction puzzles
Puzzles centered on placing geometric objects or structures rather than just shading or numbering.

### V.A. Light / visibility objects
- **Akari**  
  Place bulbs with line-of-sight illumination and adjacency counts.

### V.B. Bridges / graph edges between nodes
- **Hashiwokakero**  
  Connect numbered islands with 0–2 bridges per pair; bridges do not cross; all islands connected.

### V.C. Movable tokens
- **Satogaeri**  
  Move circles into countries.
- **Yosenabe**  
  Move circles into gray areas by straight arrows.

### V.D. Shape growth / evolutionary blocks
- **Evolomino**  
  Place square cells to form blocks on arrows; later blocks extend earlier ones by one square without rotation/reflection.

---

A puzzle can belong to one main family above, but also be described by secondary rule features.

## B. Uses outlined rooms/regions explicitly

## C. Requires global connectivity of a color/object network
- **Heyawake** — white connected
- **Hitori** — white connected
- **Kurodoko** — white connected
- **Kurotto** — local black extensions, not global
- **LITS** — shaded connected
- **Nurikabe** — black connected
- **Nurimisaki** — white connected
- **Nuritwin** — shaded connected
- **Hashiwokakero** — all islands connected
- **Akari** — all white cells illuminated, not connectivity
- **Usowan** — white connected

## D. Forbids orthogonally adjacent black/shaded cells
- **Heyawake**
- **Hitori**
- **Kurodoko**
- **Usowan**
- **Yajilin**  
  Also black cells cannot touch.

## E. Forbids 2×2 monochromatic/shaded blocks
- **LITS**
- **Nurikabe** — black 2×2 forbidden
- **Nurimeizu** — black and white cannot cover 2×2 or larger squares
- **Nurimisaki** — neither black nor white may form 2×2 or larger
- **Nuritwin** — no 2×2 shaded

## F. Strong shape-equivalence rules
- **Chained Block** — no duplicate size-and-shape blocks in a chain, considering rotations/reflections same
- **Double Choco** — white and gray areas in a block must match in shape
- **Evolomino** — successive blocks differ by one square without rotation/flipping
- **LITS** — tetromino identity matters; rotated/reflected same shape
- **Sashigane** — all regions are one-cell-wide L-shapes
- **Shikaku** — all regions rectangles
- **Choco Banana** — black components rectangles/squares; white components must not be

## G. Uses directional clues (arrows, wind, visibility)
- **Evolomino**
- **Hebi**
- **Makaro**
- **Nagareru**
- **Satogaeri**
- **Sashigane**
- **Yajilin**
- **Yosenabe**

# Compact classification by primary solving action

## Shade / color cells
Akari, Chained Block, Choco Banana, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Kurotto, LITS, Norinori, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki, Nurikabe, Nuritwin, Shakashaka, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Usowan, Yajilin

## Draw a loop
Dotchi-Loop, Masyu, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Slitherlink, Suraromu, Yajilin

## Connect / route paths
Hashiwokakero, Numberlink, Pencils, Satogaeri, Yosenabe, Nurimeizu

## Divide into regions
Double Choco, Five Cells, Fillomino, Sashigane, Shikaku

## Place numbers/symbols
Evolomino, Fillomino, Hebi, Juosan, Makaro, Nansuke, Ripple Effect, Sudoku

---

# Notes on hybrids
Several puzzles fit more than one branch:

- **Yajilin** = loop-drawing + black-cell shading.
- **Nurimeizu** = room shading + maze/path puzzle.
- **Fillomino** = number placement + region partition.
- **Akari** = object placement + illumination coverage.
- **Satogaeri** and **Yosenabe** = token movement + path routing.
- **Evolomino** = symbol placement + shape-growth constraint.
- **Sto-stone** = shading + gravity transformation condition.
